summary: A Harris County Texas Forest Service station; sources disagree on whether its tower came from here or near Conroe, and the tower now stands at the Texas Forestry Museum in Lufkin.

facts.design: 100-foot fire tower (per Texas Highways and Bowman)
facts.status_note: The tower now overlooks the Texas Forestry Museum grounds in Lufkin, Angelina County, not the East River site.

events.note: Texas Highways says the 100-foot tower was built in 1936; Bowman says towers such as the Lufkin one were built by the Civilian Conservation Corps in 1936. Whether this tower came from East River is disputed.
A March 1974 newspaper item says a 100-foot tower will be built on the proposed museum site and remain Texas Forest Service property
Bowman says the Lufkin tower was moved from its site near Conroe in 1976
Texas Forestry Museum opened in Lufkin

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Texas Highways and Bowman agree on a 1936 build date for towers like this one, though Bowman's sentence is about towers in general. The 1974 newspaper item speaks of a tower to be built on the museum site, which does not fit a 1936 tower moved in 1976. Both are recorded; no build date for the East River station itself was found.

notes_for_editor: This record covers the original East River station as the brief asks. The museum tower already has its own story and research file (us-tx-east-river-at-texas-forestry-museum), and the two overlap. Origin is disputed: the Forest Lookouts East River page is in Harris County, while Texas Highways and Bowman say the Lufkin tower came from near Conroe. The 1974 item says a tower would be built, not moved. No source read describes the East River site today. The firelookout.org Texas list that the record cites was not read in this pass, so it is not cited. The Bowman access note is from his column, which may be dated. No photos found.
